gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the 'drives included' NAS options come with fixed drives. Synology's BeeStation and BeeStation Plus each have one built-in drive with no RAID. Their only expansion is the USB-A and USB-C ports for external drives, and Blackvoid's review says the internal drive is fixed and the whole unit is replaced if it fails. For the Buffalo LinkStation 720D, the only replacement drive Buffalo lists is its own OP-HDBST-3Y series. By contrast, Synology's diskless 2025 Plus models (DS225+, DS425+) running DSM 7.3 accept unvalidated third-party hard drives, though M.2 storage pools and cache still need drives on Synology's compatibility list.
standout_why: ChatGPT's saved chat got no search results at all, so there are no cited rival pages. Its answer showed two catalog cards (Synology DS224+, UGREEN DXP4800 Plus) and asked whether the shopper wanted drives included. It said nothing about which drives each box takes, whether a pre-filled unit's drive can be swapped or mirrored, or which camera and UPS add-ons work with which model. Every compatibility fact below is therefore missing from what the shopper saw.
decides: This confirms the split our page should make. If you want to start with a drive inside, the BeeStation or BeeStation Plus is plug-and-go. But it has one fixed drive with no RAID, and the extra storage it takes is an external USB drive. Only the Plus works with BeeCamera, and the BeeStation 4 TB (BST150-4T) is excluded. If you want drives included but mirrored, Buffalo's LS720D ships with RAID already set up (RAID 0/1/JBOD), but Buffalo lists only its own OP-HDBST-3Y drives for that model. If you want to choose your own drives, a diskless DS225+ on DSM 7.3 now takes third-party hard drives (M.2 still needs listed drives). The UGREEN DH2300 and DH4300 Plus also take SATA drives, but I couldn't confirm UGREEN's list from its own pages.

findings.label: Compatible replacement drives
findings.note: This is the only compatible drive listed on the maker page. The page links to a related item, 'Replacement Hard Drives for TeraStation TS1200D and TS1400D and LinkStation 220, 420, and 720'. The page says nothing either way about third-party drives.

findings.label: RAID levels and drives included
findings.value: LS720: RAID 0/1/JBOD; LS710: none; drives come pre-installed with RAID already set up
findings.note: Models listed: LS720D0402 (4 TB), LS720D0802 (8 TB), LS720D1602 (16 TB), all 2-bay. LS710D0201/0401/0801 are 1-bay.

findings.label: Supported cameras (BeeCamera)
findings.value: Up to 4 cameras: Synology CC400W (Wi-Fi), BC500, BC510, TC500, TC510 (PoE)
findings.note: The page says BeeStation Plus is required for BeeCamera. Local recording needs the cameras and BeeStation Plus on the same local network. Guest Wi-Fi, device isolation or VLAN segmentation may need router changes.

findings.label: Camera support
findings.note: Inferred from the maker's line that 'BeeStation Plus is required for BeeCamera'. bee.synology.com also lists home monitoring and Plex only under BeeStation Plus.

findings.label: Built-in drive and expansion
findings.value: 1 built-in drive, no RAID (4 TB models use HAT3300-4T, 8 TB uses HAT3310-8T); USB-A and USB-C ports are for external storage, which BeeStation can back up automatically
findings.note: FAQ: 'Data safety comes from backups, not RAID.' The page does not describe any internal drive swap. For Plex, the Plus can index media moved to an external USB drive.

findings.label: Memory (correction to our current page)
findings.note: Synology's comparison lists BeeStation as Realtek RTD1619B with 2 GB DDR4 and BeeStation Plus as Intel Celeron J4125 with 4 GB DDR4. Our current row says 1 GB.

findings.label: Ports, client OS and network limits
findings.value: 1× USB-A 3.2 Gen 1, 1× USB-C 3.2 Gen 1, 1× 1GbE; no Wi-Fi; desktop software needs Windows 10 build 19041+ / Windows 11 / macOS 12.3+; 3-year warranty
findings.note: The USB ports are for external storage, not for transferring files from a computer. Signing in to the apps without internet is not supported, but local access by private IP or SMB works. The store page showed no price.

findings.label: Drive replaceability
findings.value: Internal drive is fixed; on failure the whole unit is replaced
findings.source_title: Synology Beestation Plus review (Luka Manestar, Blackvoid, 11 July 2025)
findings.note: Luka Manestar: 'The internal drive is fixed, and there are no tools provided to open the device or replace the drive' and 'the entire unit is replaced rather than just the drive.' Synology's own pages neither say this nor contradict it.

findings.label: Third-party drive support
findings.value: 25 model-year DiskStation Plus, Value and J series on DSM 7.3 support installing and pooling non-validated third-party drives; M.2 storage pools and cache still require drives on Synology's compatibility list (HCL)
findings.note: Quoted from the maker's press release and footnote. The DS225+ is a 2025 Plus-series model.
